note: The mouth room in the stack's foot (docs/future/19 'The mouth room', F16's mouth; src/world/stack/mouth.js): a zone (docs/26-zones.md) entered by the cave mouth's card at the back of the cleft once the causeway stands. The spring cave's chamber field (src/world/spring/cave-field.js) with two passages cut off it (src/world/stack/mouth-field.js), meshed by surface nets in a worker and drawn by a second cave pass (src/render/passes/cave.js). Its floor is above every tide; the rock pool in it stays (the tide's rise and fall in it is a later touch).
depthNote: The cleft over the way in, as the cave sees it: its chimney's top this far over the floor, open to the sky (the light comes down it). The room sits behind the cleft's back, its floor at the apron's height (the land recipe's stack.apron.heightM).
shapeNote: The spring cave's shape fields (recipes/world/spring-cave.json shapeNote), in the mouth's frame: x into the stack from the cleft's back, z across (to your left as you come in), y up from the floor. arch and rubble: the two passages, each from its root `at` along `dir` (unit [x, z]) for lengthM, halfWidthM either side, under an arched roof heightM high. The arch's ends blind past the light (it stays closed until the Hollow); the rubble's is filled with fallen rock.
viewNote: As the spring cave's (spring-cave.json viewNote): you come in under the cleft and stand arriveM in, the view turned arriveTurnDeg off straight behind you.
lightNote: As the spring cave's (spring-cave.json lightNote), the hole being the cleft's open top. lantern: the old lantern once lit, a real point light (Matt, November 1, 2026: the cave must look its best with it lit): cd candela at lightK from its flame (a bright hurricane lantern; an oil lamp is near 10), flickering by flicker at about flickerHz, whatever the hour; its sight of the rock baked (bake below), so ledges and the arch's lip throw soft shadows; glassNits: its horn panes' glow; bounce: the share of its light carried round the walls as a warm fill gathered round it; scatter: the cave air's scatter per meter, the glow round the flame; glint: its flame mirrored in wet stone. figure.lampFill: the share of the lantern's light on the walker that comes back to them off the walls close round, as their fill. It is the light the walker wakes to below later (F16).
lookNote: Linear albedos (the palette paints them at the tonemap): the rock and floor as the spring cave's; lantern, lanternRim: the old lantern's iron body and its rust; glass: its horn panes; note: the lamplighter's paper; soot: the ring round the arch; iron: the hook; stone: the rubble. water: the rock pool, with no glow of its own.
thingsNote: Where the things lie (mouth frame): the old lantern on its side at `at` (radiusM, heightM; tapM how far past it a tap still finds it), the note beside it, the hook on the wall fromArchM along the wall from the arch's side at heightM, the soot ring round the arch's opening (radiusM thick), the rubble's stones heaped in its passage (each dug stretch clears its share, front first), and the way out under the cleft (door: within tapM of the arrival spot).
bakeNote: Light baked into the rock once in the worker (src/world/stack/mouth-field.js bakeLight): for each vertex, lifted liftM off the rock, how much it sees of each spot the lantern can be (on the floor, on its hook), marched through the field to within lampClearM of the flame, the shadow's edge softened by penumbra (larger: harder) with steps between minStepM and maxStepM; and its ambient occlusion from the open air at the distances aoM out along its normal (each counting 0.7 of the one before), aoStrength how dark the deepest hollows go.

words.below: In under the stack. Cold, and the sea loud behind you.
words.door: Daylight down the cleft, and the road beyond.
words.lanternCold: An old lantern, cold. There's oil in it still.
words.lanternLit: The old lantern, lit. A hook by the arch would take it.
words.lanternHung: The old lantern on its hook by the arch. Its light keeps the dark back.
words.lit: The wick takes. A small warm light, and the walls close round it.
words.hung: It hangs by the arch. The dark past it seems to draw back a little.
words.note: A folded paper, weighted with a stone, in an old hand.
words.arch: An arch at the back of the cave, ringed with soot, and scratched signs on its stones. Something moves just past the light. Not with empty hands.
words.archSeen: Not with empty hands. A staff, perhaps: driftwood and cord.
words.archShut: Not yet. Not with empty hands, and not today.
words.rubble: A passage off the cave, choked with fallen rock.
words.rubbleDug: A passage off the cave, part dug out.
words.rubbleEnd: Dug back as far as it goes for now. The rock beyond is packed too hard.
words.dug: You work a stretch of rock loose and stack it by the wall.
words.dugToday: Enough for one visit. Your arms say so.
